newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary wheat futures up on export talk.
newsitem.headline: Hungary wheat futures up on export talk.

text.p: Maize futures rose on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Friday, while milling wheat futures were lifted by talk of potential export sales to Serbia, traders said.
March maize ended 300 forints higher at 17,900 forints per tonne. July, October and December gained 100 to 300 forints to close at 17,000, 18,000 and 18,750 respectively.

Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle Rt said the rise reflected speculative activity and a lack of deliveries. But large carry-over stocks from 1996 were likely to put maize prices under pressure in the longer term.

Traders said wheat futures, which had recently fallen on the prospect of a 500,000 tonne surplus from the 1996 crop, were boosted by market talk that Serbia was likely to need substantial amounts of imported wheat.
But they added that a build-up of large flour stocks had prompted some mills to stop production, which was likely to push wheat prices down if new export markets were not found soon.
Milling wheat futures rose by 200 to 400 forints per tonne. May was at 23,460 forints, up 400, while December also added 400 to finish at 21,500.
Lot size is 20,000 kg for all contracts.
